I am going to report this clinic for lying.

On April 28, 2026, we took our 3-week-old kitten, Athlas, to the Aviam veterinary clinic for a general check-up, as we noticed he hadn't eaten for about two hours, which worried us.

We want to state for the record that, before this visit, the kitten was in generally stable condition, considering his circumstances, given that he came from a litter affected by feline viral herpes (feline respiratory complex). In fact, he was the healthiest kitten in the entire litter. Before going to the clinic, the kitten was eating well, breathing better, and showing an active and age-appropriate demeanor.

During the consultation, we believe several inappropriate procedures were performed on an animal of such a young age:

1. An antiparasitic treatment for fleas was administered despite the kitten being only 3 weeks old, a potentially toxic and inappropriate treatment for such a small kitten.

2. A thermometer was inserted rectally, causing a high level of stress. We consider it important to note that feline herpesvirus can reactivate and worsen the animal's condition in stressful situations, weakening its immune system.

3. When attempting to feed the kitten formula, it aspirated, expelling milk from its nose, a situation that had not occurred before the handling performed at the clinic.

Following this visit, the kitten's condition deteriorated significantly, and it died the next day, April 29, 2026. We believe that the procedures performed during the consultation could have seriously contributed to the decline in its health and constitute possible veterinary negligence.

We would also like to state that the kitten had previously been examined at a veterinary clinic in Lleida, where the veterinarian expressly indicated that, due to its young age (3 weeks), it should not yet be handled or treated with medication, antiparasitics, vaccines, or other similar procedures.

Therefore, we are filing this complaint so that the events that occurred can be investigated and the corresponding responsibilities determined.

THEY KILLED OUR 3-WEEK-OLD KITTEN!!!!!! I'm leaving my review here because what they did to our kitten is NEGLIGENCE, there's no other way to describe it. This kitten was fine before; he ate, relieved himself, and walked. He was healthy. We rescued him from a farm where it wasn't safe for him to grow up. Anyway, we took him to the vet yesterday, Wednesday, April 28th, for a check-up to see if he needed more food or if he was simply fine. Then the vet we saw (a blonde woman) started handling him roughly, and then when she tried to feed him, the kitten choked on the milk, and it came out of his nose. From then on, everything worsened because his breathing became irregular, then he had apneas, and he wasn't well. His mucous membranes became pale, and today, April 29th, he died. PLEASE DO NOT TAKE YOUR ANIMALS THERE OR AT LEAST THINK TWICE.

We had Duna operated on a few months ago and we are extremely happy with the treatment, the friendly approach, and her recovery. You can always contact them with anything and they respond immediately. Thank you so much, ladies!

Excellent experience at Aviam Veterinaris. We took our husky in for neutering and tumor removal, and everything was perfect from start to finish. The service was professional, friendly, and very careful.

We especially want to highlight Carla, the veterinarian, for her dedication, clarity in explaining everything, and the care she showed our dog. His recovery was excellent, and we felt supported throughout the entire process. These very positive reviews are well-deserved. Everything went very well. Without a doubt, this veterinary clinic is highly recommended.

Anabel and Carla, thank you for the care Yoko and I received. Thank you for the daily post-operative care, since Yoko pulled out her stitches, and for the patience and kindness with which you treated us. 🩵 …

I took my cat to the emergency vet for the first time for a urinary obstruction, and at 5 pm they told me he needed to stay and that they would call me around 7:00 or 7:30 pm to pick him up, without telling me what they were going to do or the prices. I arrived before they called me; the receptionist wasn't there. There was a woman who had also come in for an emergency at 5 pm and wasn't seen until 8 pm. Her dog was vomiting everywhere, poor thing 😥. Then the doctor came and told me my cat needed to be admitted and that it would cost €50 to keep him there overnight because they had to do more tests. All this without ever asking if I had enough money. So when I went to pay, SURPRISE! They charged me €302 for a couple of tests and medication, plus the visit, which was supposed to be €40? 😱 That's outrageous! I'm unemployed, and they've left me with no money in my account because they didn't tell me the prices of the tests they were going to do. Otherwise, most of them wouldn't have been done because, according to the doctor before charging me, the animal wasn't doing too badly 🤦‍♀️. Of course, we'll continue going to our usual vet; she tells us the prices of the services before charging us and works within our budget since it's a cooperative with very affordable prices and the staff are super nice.
They have good communication with the animals and very good clientele and are friendly.

My dog ​​is 11 years old today, and she's celebrating thanks to them. My little dog, Kira, came in for a checkup because she had a possible severe ear infection. When they analyzed her symptoms, they realized her ear canal was about to rupture due to pyometra, and she could die at any moment if her body couldn't handle it. Because of a misdiagnosis by another vet, my dog ​​had been suffering in silence for three weeks. She underwent emergency surgery without hesitation, and they were incredibly attentive from the moment she arrived until she was discharged. Simply put, thank you; they gave me my life back.

(The vet showed me images from the operating room so I could see the severity of her condition and why she had referred her for emergency surgery.)
Highly professional and attentive to the animals

Competent and professional, a true benchmark for me and my dogs. They operated on my Nube, and the care they provided was extraordinary. I will always be grateful for their help and for saving my dog.

I took my kitten to Aviam for her spaying, trusting that she was in good hands. However, after the surgery on the 19th, I noticed something wasn't right; she wouldn't eat or drink and was lethargic. We returned to the clinic on the 21st because the wound was open, and although they told us the internal muscles were fine, they only sutured the outside. The next day, the 22nd, we had to go to the emergency room because her condition worsened; something internal was protruding.

In the emergency room, they discovered that the internal muscles hadn't been properly closed and that there was an infection. My kitten suffered greatly, and so did I, seeing her like that. I feel that all of this could have been avoided if they had done their job properly from the beginning. This experience has been very painful and has shattered my trust in Aviam. I advise other pet owners to be cautious when choosing where to take their loved ones.

Always seek a second opinion and don't let yourselves be driven by desperation in the moment. I find it appalling when a supposedly charitable organization takes advantage of the situation to exert pressure and try to profit from it.

On Monday, our 4-month-old kitten fell from the balcony. We called several veterinarians to compare prices for the diagnosis, and they quoted us between €250 and €300. Then I remembered Aviam. The telephone service was good; we spoke with the vet first, and then the other woman at reception, who handles the billing and payment, took over. She gave us an estimated price of around €100-€150 and said the consultation would be €37 (in the end, she charged us €58, without us noticing because the invoice arrived later by email). I understand it's a business and that we have to pay for their services, and that there might be additional things like sedation or blood work that weren't in the initial estimate but were needed during the visit, and obviously those are added to the bill. But if she tells us the consultation is €37, I don't think it's right that she charges us €20 more.

Over the phone, he told us about a traumatologist he could refer us to if surgery was needed, and that he would give us a good price, giving us examples of other quotes (he said that another cat had been quoted €7,000 at veterinary hospitals and that his traumatologist had quoted them between €700 and €1,400), which sounded a bit like a sales pitch.
Anyway, we thought the price was good for the consultation and diagnosis, and my partner took Sharma to the vet a few hours later.
The care was wonderful; they took all the time in the world and treated our little one very well. She had broken her hip.
When it came time to pay, they started telling us that it was going to heal incorrectly and that surgery was necessary because otherwise, she wouldn't be able to defecate and we would have to keep taking her to the vet to have her stool removed for the rest of her life. This sounded increasingly strange to me because there are many complications that can arise from a hip fracture in a cat, but this wasn't one of them. But of course, you're in that situation and you trust a professional.

When my boyfriend wanted to go home and asked them to charge him, the receptionist intervened. She started telling him to wait, that she was going to text the orthopedic surgeon on WhatsApp. She kept him there for another hour (a full hour). My boyfriend kept asking her to charge him and to let us know what the surgeon thought when she got back to us. He said she would consult with me and we would let you know, but there was no way he could leave because she wouldn't charge him. Then the orthopedic surgeon called her. He asked if the client was there, and she said yes. Then she left the room so my boyfriend couldn't hear the conversation. This gave us a feeling of a lack of transparency. She did this several times during different calls she had with him.

So, suddenly, she comes to us with a quote of €880. She says we have to pay it upfront, under the table, and to her, instead of to the orthopedic surgeon when the surgery takes place. That's when all the alarm bells started ringing.
She pressured my boyfriend a lot, telling him the operation had to be that Thursday or it would be too late. Then she extended it to the following Tuesday and told us we could pay half now and half on the day of the operation.
After much insistence and putting her in an awkward position (using sales tactics like the silent treatment), she finally took his money and left.
Well, guess what: the cat doesn't need the operation and is perfectly fine going to the bathroom. We would have put her through unnecessary anesthesia and surgery.
Three days later, she contacted my partner by phone, and when he told her we had consulted other veterinarians, that the hip heals on its own, especially in such a small cat, and that surgery wasn't necessary, the woman just said, "Okay, goodbye," and the call ended.
As I said, I understand it's a business and they have to make money, but there have been many unnecessary situations during this whole process.

I want to express my deepest gratitude to Sara from Aviam Veterinaris and the team at the Vetalliance clinic in Badalona. My cat, Tuki, suffered a serious accident at home that left him with a broken jaw, two fractures in his right leg, and …

I've been going to this vet for years and they're all great, both the administrative staff and Carla, the vet, who's a sweetheart. They're not impatient at all; they treat your dogs with so much love. I highly recommend them... thank you, Carla, for treating my dogs so well! 💋💋 …
